- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ -0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to match true decline.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates true price at end of horizon; add 1–3% to final 5–7 days of forecast to account for momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model overfits to recent trends; dampen forecast volatility by 10–20% in next 3–5 days.
